findings.title: Empty updateMany does not bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt and can throw
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) specifically to refresh SelectedCalendar.updatedAt after writing calendar cache. Prisma only applies @updatedAt when the update payload changes at least one field; an empty data object is either a no-op (updatedAt stays stale) or an invalid updateMany invocation that throws. This runs on the Google webhook/cache-refresh path after the cache upsert, so a throw fails the refresh even though the cache write succeeded, and a no-op means the timestamp this change exists to maintain is never updated.

findings.title: Deleting cache does not refresh connected-calendar status
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess callback. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The settings page passes onChanged through, which is often undefined and is not the connectedCalendars query. After a successful delete the dropdown still renders the previous cacheUpdatedAt and still offers “Delete cached data” until a full reload.

findings.title: Backfill stamps every existing cache row as updated at deploy time
findings.body: The new NOT NULL updatedAt column is added with DEFAULT NOW() and no backfill from a real write time. Every pre-existing CalendarCache row, including expired ones, gets the migration timestamp. getCacheStatusByCredentialIds then takes MAX(updatedAt) with no expiresAt filter, so the new UI shows “Last updated” as the deploy time and treats expired legacy cache as present for every credential that has ever had a row.

findings.title: Webhook tunnel script is macOS-only and writes the wrong .env
findings.body: sed -i '' is BSD sed syntax and fails on GNU sed (Linux). ENV_FILE is ../.env relative to the process cwd, not the script directory, so bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root creates or edits a .env outside the repository instead of the app env file. The script then reports success while GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was never set where the app reads it.

findings.title: No tests for cache deletion authorization or status query
findings.body: deleteCache is an authenticated mutation that deletes every CalendarCache row for a credential after a userId ownership check, and connected calendars now depend on getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. There are no tests for a matching owner, a credential owned by another user, a missing id, or the groupBy status mapping (including expired rows). A regression in the where clause would either 500 the calendar settings page or let one user wipe another user’s cache with no CI signal.
